5671.a: It is the move of the employees of a government entity from the Civil Service Law, or any other employment system, to the Labor Law; or the change of their workers' coverage from the employment regulation applied to them to another employment regulation, as a result of the transition decision issued by the Council of Ministers approving the transition.

5672.a: It is the transfer of the affiliation of the employees and workers of the Ministry of Health from the public sector to the Health Holding Company, which is a company that has an independent legal personality and independent financial accountability, and is fully owned by the State, as a result of the issuance of the privatization decision.

5673.q: Will the Health Holding Company replace the Ministry of Health?
5673.a: No, the Health Holding Company will not replace the Ministry of Health. The company will take over the operational side that the Ministry used to carry out before, while the Ministry will remain responsible for the regulatory and supervisory aspects.

5677.q: What is the Health Holding Company and what is its work?
5677.a: The Health Holding Company is a company fully owned by the State, which has an independent legal personality and independent financial accountability. It takes over the provision of health care through Health Clusters affiliated with it, which provide comprehensive and integrated health care within their defined geographic areas. It was established under Council of Ministers Decision No. (469) dated 19/8/1443 AH.

5678.a: A Health Cluster is a unified institutional system that has an integrated and interconnected network of facilities providing health care services. The Health Cluster is the entity responsible for everything that affects the health of the community and individuals within its defined geographic area, where it works to support a living environment that promotes health, and provides comprehensive health care services of all kinds, with a focus on the quality of the services and not only on the facilities that provide them.

5674.q: Will the number of Health Clusters be increased?
5674.a: The number of Health Clusters is currently 20 Health Clusters. There is no plan at the present time to increase the number of Health Clusters.

5669.q: What is meant by an employee?
5669.a: It is every natural person who holds a public civil position, and is subject to the Civil Service Law or to any other employment system, together with the civil retirement system.

5670.q: What is meant by a worker?
5670.a: It is every natural person who works for the benefit of a government entity or an administrative entity and under its management, and is subject to the Labor Law and the GOSI (General Organization for Social Insurance) system. This is what is referred to in the Ministry as self-operated staff.

5751.q: What is the role of the Ministry's Diwan in the process of transferring staff?
5751.a: The Ministry's Diwan supervises the process of transferring the staff targeted for transfer, in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD), and approves the comparison criteria in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), in a way that ensures the achievement of the objectives and the fulfillment of the requirements of the current stage.

5683.q: Will the basic salary or the total salary change upon transfer?
5683.a: Upon the transfer of the employee/worker, a work contract will be concluded for him that ensures that the basic salary and the total wage are not less than what he was receiving before the transfer.

5739.q: I am an employee (civil service). Will there be an increase in my salary upon transfer, and what is the increase?
5739.a: Upon the transfer of the employee, a work contract is concluded with him that ensures that the basic and actual wage is not less than the salary he was receiving before the transfer.

5679.q: What will the transfer request contain in terms of salary?
5679.a: The transfer request is updated based on the current total salary approved by the Ministry of Health, to make sure it reflects any changes that occurred to promotions, allowances, wages, or benefits.

5684.q: Why is there a difference in salaries between the civil service and self-operation?
5684.a: The transfer requests for the employees were developed based on their current status, with emphasis on applying Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), which states that the basic salary or the total salary of the employee after the transfer must not be less than what he was receiving before the transfer. This is what was applied to all civil service and self-operated staff.

5681.q: What are the allowances that the new contract will include upon the transfer of the Health Clusters?
5681.a: A work contract will be concluded for the employee/worker that includes the housing allowance and the transportation allowance only, in a way that ensures that the total salary is not less than the total salary that the employee/worker was previously receiving.

5682.q: Will the housing allowance be paid annually upon the transfer of the Health Clusters?
5682.a: Upon the transfer, the housing allowance will be paid to the employees on a monthly basis.

5686.q: Does the transfer affect the salaries and allowances?
5686.a: All monthly allowances have been merged into the new total salary after the transfer, in a way that ensures that the total salary of the employee/worker does not decrease, in accordance with what was stated in Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

5687.q: What are the allowances included in the total salary?
5687.a: All fixed monthly allowances approved by the Ministry of Health have been included in the calculation of the new total salary, so that the total monthly and basic salary of any employee/worker will not be less upon his transfer. All monthly allowances have been merged into the total salary.

5688.q: Will the excellence allowance continue after the transfer?
5688.a: The excellence allowance has been replaced by an annual reward granted to distinguished employees and workers based on performance evaluation.

5689.q: Has the full-time allowance been included in the salary after the transfer?
5689.a: All monthly allowances have been included in the total salary after the transfer, in a way that ensures that the total salary of the staff does not decrease, in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

5690.q: Will there be a supervision allowance?
5690.a: All monthly allowances that are paid in accordance with the system have been included in the total salary after the transfer, in a way that ensures that the total salary of the staff does not decrease, in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616). As for the supervision allowance, it is an allowance paid on an annual basis and is not counted among the monthly allowances.

5692.q: Will there be a leadership allowance?
5692.a: All monthly allowances have been included in the total salary after the transfer, in a way that ensures that the total salary of the staff does not decrease, in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

5691.q: Will previous entitlements, such as the excellence allowance for the years 2024 and 2025, be paid?
5691.a: The Ministry of Health will continue to pay the entitlements of the staff related to the previous procedures. In the event that there are entitlements that were not paid upon the transfer, they will be paid within the service termination procedures and in accordance with the regulations approved in the Ministry.

5693.q: Are there any deductions other than the GOSI deduction in the transfer request sent to the transferred employees?
5693.a: There are no deductions other than the statutory GOSI (General Organization for Social Insurance) deduction.

5694.q: Will the criteria for receiving allowances change after the transition?
5694.a: If the employee's contract is in effect at the Ministry of Health, the current allowance policies apply to him, according to the entitlement before signing the contract. After the transition, the policies applied in the Health Cluster apply to him.

5696.q: Will I receive a transition request, or will I receive the contract directly?
5696.a: The targeted Health Clusters, together with the Ministry of Health, are resuming the transition stage gradually. Transition requests will be sent to all staff who pass the selection criteria and bases, and they can accept or reject them.

5723.q: What are the criteria under which an employee's transition request is accepted? And which legal article provides for them?
5723.a:
In accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), the Ministry of Health has committed to setting fair and clear criteria to determine the bases of selection, in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, based on the following criteria:
Those covered by the health regulation: qualifications, experience, performance evaluation, classification by the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties.
The administrative staff: qualifications, experience, and performance evaluation.

5703.q: Will there be an exception for employees whose evaluation is lower than 3?
5703.a: Performance evaluation is one of the criteria for selection among staff and not the only criterion. Staff targeted for transfer are dealt with based on the approved selection criteria and bases, in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

5727.q: The selection criteria and bases include qualifications; are there any excluded qualifications? And what is the minimum approved qualification?
5727.a: There are no excluded qualifications, and there is no minimum qualification for the transition. The main requirement in the qualification criterion is that the qualification matches the placement requirements for the current job.

5701.q: Will the skills required for the transition be specified in the non-medical and administrative specialties, such as finance, quality, engineering, and other specialties?
5701.a: Employees are transferred when they pass the selection criteria and bases, in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development. A framework of the skills needed for each job role will be specified, in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

5707.q: Will the contract be based on the self-operated and civil service qualification?
5707.a: The contract will be based on the current job title that the employee/worker holds, taking into account the requirements of the current job in terms of qualifications and experience. If a job becomes available that requires higher qualifications, it will be announced through internal recruitment, where anyone who meets the required conditions for the job will be able to apply for it. Candidates will be selected according to clear criteria to ensure transparency and fairness in the selection process.

5724.q: When the job offers are sent to start the transition procedures, will the job titles change?
5724.a: Job offers for the transition will be sent with the employee's same current job title.

5715.q: My job was changed from technician to administrator; will I transition according to the previous job or the current job?
5715.a: Job offers are sent based on the employee's data registered in the Mawared system, and the current title will be taken into account. Any changes that occurred to the job title, promotions, or allowances will be taken into consideration before sending the transition request, in order to ensure the accuracy of the request and its fulfillment of the entitled benefits, in accordance with what Council of Ministers Decision No. (616) provides.

5717.q: For technician employees who work in administrative jobs, will they return to technical jobs through training before the contract?
5717.a: The contract will be based on the employee's current title, and his case is evaluated according to the approved promotion policy, based on the available qualifications and experience.

5725.q: For an employee who holds an extra qualification, will he transition with the current qualification or the extra one?
5725.a: An employee who holds an extra qualification will be transitioned and appointed to the same current job according to the qualification registered in the system, and not on the extra qualification.

5718.q: Regarding employees who will be sent on scholarship to complete their studies in the coming period, will the contract be based on the new certificate?
5718.a: They will be contacted after their return and after they start their work, to coordinate the transition mechanism and provide them with the appropriate transition request according to their new qualifications.

5706.q: What is the type of contracts for civil service employees after the transition?
5706.a: Their contracts will be subject to the Labor Law and the GOSI system, and according to the wages and benefits in force.

5765.q: What is the duration of the job contract that is sent?
5765.a: The contract was built in accordance with Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), and its duration is two years, renewed automatically for a similar period unless one of the two parties notifies the other of its wish not to renew.

5720.q: What is the mechanism for renewing the contracts?
5720.a: The entity to which the transfer is made is committed to an employment contract for a period of no less than two years, and the principle is that the contract is renewed with the same wage and benefits, except where there is a reason that requires otherwise.

5712.q: What will happen after the end of the contract period? (after the end of the two years)?
5712.a: The employees are the essential nucleus of the transition, as the contracts are renewed automatically unless there is a legal reason that prevents that, affirming the continuity of the staff and the achievement of the transition goals without exception.

5733.q: For someone who has less than two years remaining before reaching the legal age of sixty, is a two-year contract concluded with him, or a contract for the period remaining until he reaches sixty years of age?
5733.a: An employment contract will be concluded for all employees who pass the selection criteria and bases for a period of no less than two years, and the principle is that the contract is renewed with the same wage and benefits, unless there is a legal reason that prevents that.

5767.q: Is there a probation period in the contract?
5767.a: No, the contract does not include a probation period.

5719.q: Will the working hours change upon the transition?
5719.a: The transition request includes clauses that clarify the weekly working hours in line with the Labor Law approved at the level of the Kingdom.

5729.q: How are employees assigned in other regions dealt with? Are they returned to the staffing structure? Or do they continue at the place of assignment?
5729.a: The transfer to the Health Clusters is based on the employee's current place of work, regardless of the staffing structure.

5708.q: I work in a company affiliated with one of the hospitals; am I among the targeted categories in the transition?
5708.a: Staff contracted in affiliated companies are not among the targeted categories in the current transition process, as their employment contract follows the operating company they work for.

5710.q: What are the requirements from the employee before the job offers are sent and the contracts are signed?
5710.a: The employee's data is updated in the Mawared system, then the transition request is sent via the ministerial email based on the information registered in the system.

5764.q: I am an employee on leave and I have not received a transition request; what is the reason?
5764.a: Transition requests are currently sent to employees whose status appears as active in the Mawared system. If your status is 'inactive', you will not receive a transition request.

5709.q: When will the job contract be sent after the employee accepts the transition request?
5709.a: Accepting the transition request is considered part of the job contract. To complete the legal procedures, a text message will arrive from the Qiwa platform to document the contract in accordance with the Labor Law.

5769.q: How can I accept the job contract through the "Qiwa" platform?
5769.a: You can do this by logging in to your account on (Qiwa Individuals), then going to the (Services) menu and choosing (Job Contracts), where you can review the sent contract and take the acceptance action.

5770.q: Can I modify the contract terms before accepting it?
5770.a: You cannot modify the details of the sent contract; the decision to accept or reject is made based on the version currently uploaded on the platform.

5700.q: What will happen to Civil Service employees? Will they be moved to contracts, and is the transition mandatory or optional?
5700.a: If the employee meets the selection criteria and bases, he is given the choice between transitioning or staying under the current systems. If he does not wish to transition, he is treated according to the procedures stated in the relevant laws and decisions.

5699.q: What will happen to the Civil Service employee who does not wish to transition, as well as the one who could not find another government entity to take him in? Is it possible to contract with him if he cannot be absorbed by other government entities?
5699.a: The employee who does not wish to transition has the right to transfer his services with his job, in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development and the Ministry of Finance, to any other government entity within a period not exceeding 6 months from the date the Ministry approves the employee's request not to transition and notifies him of its decision 'and it may be extended for a similar period with the Minister's approval, and only within the narrowest limits'. During this period, the employee has the right to be absent from work 'one full day per week' or 'eight hours per week' to search for another government entity to transfer to. If he is unable to transfer his services during this period, his rights and entitlements will be settled and his service will be terminated from the position he holds.

5735.q: What is the mechanism that will be applied if an employee (health practitioner) refuses to transition to the company and his service exceeds 25 years?
5735.a:
When a "Civil Service" employee passes the selection criteria and bases and his years of service exceed 25 years, and he does not wish to transition, he is given the choice between:
Referral to early retirement, in accordance with the applicable systems.
Transferring his services, in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development and the Ministry of Finance, to another government entity within a period not exceeding 6 months from the date the Ministry approves his transition request and notifies him of its decision. During this period, the employee has the right to be absent one full day per week to search for work in another government entity.
If he is unable to transfer his services during this period, his service will be terminated from the position he holds.
As for the worker subject to the "Labor and Workmen Law" who does not wish to transition, his contractual relationship is terminated and he is treated according to his rights and the regulations applicable to him.

5722.q: What is the mechanism for dealing with an employee subject to the Labor and Workmen Law who does not wish to transition?
5722.a: The employee who met the selection criteria and refused to transition will have his contractual relationship terminated, and his rights and entitlements settled in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

5711.q: Does the employee have the right to reverse his decision to reject the transition request?
5711.a: No. According to Decision (616), a set of procedures will begin to be implemented as soon as the rejection or acceptance is reported, depending on the type of employment (self-operated, Civil Service).

5702.q: What is the transition method for those whose service exceeds 25 years?
5702.a: Employees whose calculated service exceeds 25 years, who meet the selection criteria and wish to transition, will have their previous service in the Civil Pension system added to their new service in the GOSI system, in accordance with the benefits exchange system. If they do not wish to transition, they may request referral to early retirement.

5726.q: Will job offers be sent to an employee subject to the Civil Service Law who has service exceeding 25 years?
5726.a: When the employee passes the selection criteria and bases (regardless of the calculated years of service), a work contract will be concluded for him.

5713.q: Does the employee have the right to early retirement after agreeing to transition if his service is more than 25 years, and after two years have passed he wishes to retire?
5713.a: If the employee subject to the Civil Service Law passes the selection criteria and bases and wishes to transition, and his years of service are 25 years or more, he is given the choice between referral to early retirement, or adding his previous service period to his new service, in accordance with paragraphs (2-b) and (3) of Article Thirteen of Council of Ministers Decision No. (616). After the transition, the applicable regulations and laws are applied, and the service is considered continuous, and the employee can benefit from it to request early retirement later.

5721.q: I am a (Civil Service) employee who meets the transition criteria and my service is more than 25 years, and I chose early retirement. Do I have the right to conclude a contract with the Health Clusters if they need me?
5721.a: The employee who chose early retirement does not have the right to conclude a new work contract with the entity he was transferred to.

5734.q: Will the employee's civil service be merged with the GOSI system?
5734.a: Yes. If he chooses to transition and his service is included, it is handled in accordance with the approved benefits exchange system and Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), and it can be used for early retirement purposes.

5736.q: I am a (Civil Service) employee who meets the transition criteria and my service is more than 25 years, and I chose to add my service. Is the added service considered an extension of my previous service so that I can benefit from it for early retirement after the transition?
5736.a: Yes, the added service is considered an extension of the previous service, and it can be used for early retirement purposes after the transition.

5737.q: If an employee's service is 23 years (under the Civil Service Law) and he wished to transition to GOSI, then completed two additional years, does he have the right to benefit from his previous service for early retirement?
5737.a: Yes, as the service is considered continuous, and the employee can benefit from it for early retirement in accordance with the applicable systems.

5738.q: How is someone who has service in the Civil Service and the Labor Law (private sector) handled?
5738.a: The employee will be handled in accordance with the benefits exchange system between the Civil and Military Pension systems and the GOSI system, as stated in Council of Ministers Decision No. (616).

8543.q: I am a Civil Service employee. Upon resignation after privatization under Decision 616, will I be forced to complete a full 25 years in the Labor Law system in order to benefit from early retirement?
8543.a:
One of the benefits of Decision 616 is that the employee's service under the Civil Service Law is counted as complementary to his service under the Labor Law for early retirement purposes, after the transition request to the Health Cluster is accepted.
For example, if a Civil Service employee completed 20 years of service before the transition, then transitioned to the Labor Law system, the remaining period for him to benefit from early retirement would be only 5 years, in accordance with the systems applicable in the GOSI system.

8542.q: I am 59 years old and I received a transition request from the Health Cluster. Am I obligated to complete the two years mentioned in the contract, or can I retire upon reaching the age of 60?
8542.a: Transition requests issued by the Health Cluster are binding on the cluster only, and do not prevent the employee from exercising his legal right to request retirement upon reaching the age of 60, in accordance with the systems and regulations applicable in the GOSI system.

5728.q: In the case of the transition of the worker (self-operated), will his services be terminated, his record closed, and will he be re-employed with a new contract from the beginning? And will he receive his previous entitlements with self-operation, or do things continue as they are and the end-of-service benefit is calculated continuously?
5728.a: A work contract is concluded upon the transition in accordance with the job system applied there, and the applicable wages and benefits are calculated. The employee's subscription in the GOSI system is considered continuous, and his services are considered continuous with regard to the end-of-service benefit and leaves.

5731.q: How will doctors on the self-operation status be handled?
5731.a: With regard to self-operated staff (workers), according to Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), when the staff member passes the selection criteria and bases and wishes to transition, a work contract will be concluded for him that is not less than what he was receiving before the transition, with the continuation of his subscription in the GOSI system, and his services are considered continuous with regard to the end-of-service benefit and leaves.

5756.q: What is the mechanism for dealing with self-operated staff (their leaves and years of service)? And will they have new contracts and be compensated for previous service and leave balance?
5756.a: A new work contract is concluded in accordance with the job system applied there for the employee who passed the selection criteria and bases and wished to transition, and his subscription in the GOSI system continues, and his services are considered continuous with regard to the end-of-service benefit and leaves.

5704.q: What is the status of employees who fall under the wage-item system?
5704.a:
They are handled in accordance with the provisions applied to workers in Decision (616). If they meet the selection criteria and bases and wish to transition, work contracts are concluded with them, taking into account the following:
That the basic and total wage not be less than what they were receiving before the transition.
The continuation of their subscription in the GOSI system, and their service is considered continuous with regard to end-of-service and leaves.

5744.q: Will employees have any rewards upon transition?
5744.a: For staff subject to the Civil Service Law, a reward will be paid according to the text of Council of Ministers Decision No. (616), such that the reward is calculated on the basis of (16%) of his basic salary for each year of his years of service (and for each part of a year proportionally), provided that the total paid to him under this paragraph does not exceed (four) basic salaries, or on the basis of the reward due to him at the end of his service under the job system applicable to him, whichever is greater.

5742.q: How will the transition benefit be calculated, and will it affect the end-of-service benefit?
5742.a: A Civil Service employee receives a benefit in line with the text of Council of Ministers Resolution No. (616), whereby the benefit is calculated on the basis of (16%) of his basic salary for each year of his service (and for each part of a year in proportion to it), provided that the total paid to him under this paragraph does not exceed (four) basic salaries; or on the basis of the benefit due to him at the end of his service under the employment system applied to him, whichever is greater.

5705.q: I am an employee, I meet the criteria, and I wish to transition to the private sector. My previous service is less than 25 years, and after the transition I chose to add my previous service, which is subject to the Civil Pension system, to my new service, which is subject to the GOSI system. How will my financial and job-related rights be handled at retirement based on the GOSI system?
5705.a: Your financial dues, if any (secondment allowances, allowances...), are paid, in addition to a benefit calculated on the basis of (16%) of the basic salary for each year of service, and for each part of a year in proportion to it, provided that their total does not exceed (four basic salaries); or on the basis of the benefit due at the end of your service under the employment system you were following at the Ministry of Health before the transition, whichever is greater. You are compensated for your leave balance in accordance with the employment system you were following before the transition. As for the retirement pension, it is calculated in accordance with the benefits-exchange system between the Civil and Military Pension systems and the GOSI system.

5741.q: Will there be medical insurance after the transition?
5741.a: Yes, treatment of the employee, his family, and his parents will be covered within the Health Cluster network and the affiliated networks.

5746.q: Will there be an annual increment after the transition?
5746.a: The annual increment will be based on performance evaluation, and it is calculated as a percentage of the basic salary and added to the basic salary. Therefore, when it is added to the basic salary, the housing allowance and the transport allowance increase, which positively affects the end-of-service benefit and the retirement pension.

5743.q: How will the employee's annual performance evaluation work?
5743.a: The performance evaluation process will be carried out according to an approved mechanism that ensures fairness and transparency. It relies on a comprehensive (360-degree) evaluation that includes several sources, such as the direct manager, colleagues, subordinates, in addition to the beneficiaries of the service. This approach aims to measure performance in an integrated way, which helps to enhance the quality of the services provided and the continuous effort to develop them and raise their efficiency.

5745.q: Will the transition affect the promotion I am due for in the near future?
5745.a: If the promotion is due and a promotion decision was issued for it before the start of the contract, it will be counted in the new job title. Any changes to the job title, or the increase in salary, or allowances, or other changes are considered from the date the offers are sent until the date the employment contracts are concluded, in line with Council of Ministers Resolution No. (616).

5716.q: What are the career development opportunities after the transition?
5716.a: Training and development programs will be put in place to suit the nature of the work of the Health Clusters' staff and their skill and leadership needs, which helps the effectiveness of their performance and their professional advancement within their career path.

5753.q: Will there be scholarships for employees in the future?
5753.a: Yes, there is a scholarship system.

5758.q: Are there any changes regarding leave after the transition?
5758.a: After the transition, the employee is entitled to annual leave of 30 calendar days, not including the official holidays approved in the country.

5759.q: What is the reason for reducing the number of leave days?
5759.a: The number of leave days was set in line with the work laws and regulations in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

5755.q: How will the current leave balance be compensated?
5755.a:
For Civil Service staff: the employee is compensated for his leave balance and end-of-service benefit in accordance with the employment system he was following before the transition. If the balance is for the period from 1/7/1439 H until the date of the end of service, it is compensated with no more than (72) days; and if the employee has a balance prior to the date 1/7/1439 H, it is compensated with no more than a total of (180 days); and in all cases the total compensation does not exceed (180 days).
As for self-operated staff: their service is treated as continuous with regard to leave and end-of-service benefit, as the full leave balance will be transferred.

5754.q: What is the mechanism for handling compensatory leave?
5754.a: The employee must take the compensatory leave before signing the contract, as after signing the contract the compensatory leave balances will not be transferred.

5757.q: Can the employee use his leave balance after the transition request is accepted and before the employment contract is signed?
5757.a: Employees can use their leave balance at any time before the employment contract is signed, and employees are encouraged to use their available leave balance, as the employee will be compensated for his leave balance when the employment contracts are sent.

8544.q: I have a compensatory leave balance that has not been used; do I lose this balance immediately when the transition request arrives?
8544.a: A Civil Service employee who has leave days and wishes to take them is granted a grace period not exceeding (60) days between the date the transition request is accepted and the date the contract takes effect, in order to enable him to benefit from the ordinary or compensatory leave balance due to him, in accordance with the approved procedures and controls and in a way that does not affect work requirements.

5760.q: For an employee whose leave was approved in advance, is this leave cancelled after the employment contract is approved?
5760.a: If the leave starts after the contract is signed, it is counted from the new balance, and the employee must submit a new leave request.

5761.q: For employees at the health centers, are all administrative tasks and procedures such as leave and evaluations done directly through the Health Cluster, or is the employee's primary reference the direct manager at the health center where he works?
5761.a: There is no change in terms of the high-level organizational structure of the Cluster, and work continues according to the approved administrative hierarchy, and this includes the direct managers.

5762.q: Was the leave balance adjusted because of the transition?
5762.a: The leave balances were updated as a result of the periodic review for the purpose of ensuring the accuracy of the data and speeding up the processing of the request, and this is not linked to the transition process.

5763.q: Will the leave balance be adjusted in the future?
5763.a: Leave balances are updated continuously to ensure that any actual changes are reflected, out of care for the accuracy and fairness of the data, and to make sure that all balances reflect the employee's actual situation without any shortfall or error. In case of any questions about the leave balance, you can contact the Human Resources team at the Cluster you belong to in order to get the necessary clarification.

HRSD-98.q: What is the maximum number of actual working hours under the Labor Law?
HRSD-98.a: A worker may not actually be employed for more than eight hours a day if the employer adopts the daily standard, or more than forty-eight hours a week if the employer adopts the weekly standard. The actual working hours are reduced during Ramadan for Muslims so that they do not exceed six hours a day or thirty-six hours a week. (Labor Law, Article Ninety-Eight). This is a general text in the Law, and your specific working hours are stated in the transition request.

HRSD-84.q: How is the end-of-service benefit calculated under the Labor Law?
HRSD-84.a: If the work relationship ends, the employer pays the worker a benefit for his period of service calculated on the basis of half a month's wage for each of the first five years, and one month's wage for each of the following years, and the last wage is taken as the basis for the calculation, and the benefit is due for parts of a year in proportion to the time spent in work. (Labor Law, Article Eighty-Four). This is a general text, and the details of your case are determined by the systems applied to you and the approved answers in the "Rewards and Benefits" section.

HRSD-88.q: What is the statutory period for settling a worker's rights at the end of his service?
HRSD-88.a: If the worker's service ends, the employer must pay his wage and settle his rights within one week at most from the date the contractual relationship ends; but if it is the worker who ended the contract, his rights must be settled in full within a period not exceeding two weeks. (Labor Law, Article Eighty-Eight).

GOSI-1.q: What is meant by the benefits-exchange system?
GOSI-1.a: The benefits-exchange system between the Civil and Military Pension systems and the GOSI system is a system that allows a subscriber who is subject to the Civil Pension system or the Military Pension system and has a prior subscription period in the GOSI system, or vice versa, to add his subscription period in the first system to his subscription period in the latter system, in order to benefit from those periods when settling his retirement dues.

GOSI-2.q: Do the added periods qualify for entitlement to a retirement pension before reaching the age of sixty?
GOSI-2.a: The subscription periods added between the GOSI system and the Civil Pension system or the Military Pension system do not qualify for entitlement to a retirement pension before reaching the age of sixty, as the subscriber must complete the period required by the latter system to obtain that pension. As an exception to that, the added periods can be used for entitlement to the pension before reaching the age of sixty if the reasons for the addition result from transition or privatization, or if the end of service is due to death, disability, or being removed from service through coordination.

GOSI-3.q: Is it permissible to combine the retirement pension due for the added periods resulting from transition or privatization with the salary or wage?
GOSI-3.a: In the case of an addition resulting from transition or privatization, it is not permissible to combine the retirement pension due for the added periods resulting from transition or privatization with the salary or wage.
